ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, the height H between the upper and lower edges of the window is 1.6 m, the thickness of the wall is d=0.4 m, and at point P, which is a distance L=1.4 m from the wall and a distance h=0.2 m from the upper edge of the window, a person throws a small object that can be regarded as a particle horizontally with speed magnitude v. The small object passes directly through the window and lands on the horizontal ground. Take g=10 m/s2. What is the range of values of v?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, there is a point P on the right side. The small object is thrown from P to the left with horizontal speed v; the horizontal distance from P to the near side of the wall is labeled L. There is a window on the wall, the vertical height between the upper and lower edges of the window is labeled H, point P is higher than the upper edge of the window, and the vertical distance between the two is labeled h. The wall has thickness, and the bottom is labeled d with a horizontal arrow. The dashed trajectory indicates that the small object undergoes horizontal projectile motion, passes through the window, and then lands on the ground. Reasoning: Establish coordinates according to the specified method, taking the height of point P as y=0 and the vertically downward direction as positive. In horizontal projectile motion, the horizontal displacement x=vt, and the vertical falling distance y=\frac12gt^2, so when the horizontal displacement is x, y=\frac{gx^2}{2v^2}. When reaching the near side wall surface, the horizontal displacement is L=1.4 m, and the falling distance is y1=\frac{gL^2}{2v^2}=\frac{10\times1.4^2}{2v^2}=\frac{9.8}{v^2}. To enter below the upper edge of the window, it is necessary that y1>h=0.2 m, namely \frac{9.8}{v^2}>0.2, giving v^2<49, so v<7 m/s. When reaching the far side wall surface, the horizontal displacement is L+d=1.4+0.4=1.8 m, and the falling distance is y2=\frac{g(L+d)^2}{2v^2}=\frac{10\times1.8^2}{2v^2}=\frac{16.2}{v^2}. To pass out above the lower edge of the window, it is necessary that y2<h+H=0.2+1.6=1.8 m, namely \frac{16.2}{v^2}<1.8, giving v^2>9, so v>3 m/s. Combining the two conditions, the speed range is 3 m/s<v<7 m/s.
